mainTopic: רבה's three fields and נכסי מלוג; אמימר's ruling and the ברייתא on whether owning the use (קנין פירות) equals owning the thing (קנין הגוף)
overview: This amud finishes רבה's list of three fields where a wife who agreed to a sale can later say she only agreed to please her husband. The גמרא asks what the list leaves out. It rejects the idea that it leaves out the husband's other property, since there the pressure on her would be even greater. Instead it says the list leaves out נכסי מלוג, her own property that he only gets the profits of. אמימר's ruling that a sale of נכסי מלוג does nothing seems to contradict this. The first answer says אמימר meant only a sale by one spouse alone, backed by the enactment of אושא, while a sale by both or by the wife to her husband is valid. A second answer says אמימר follows רבי אלעזר, and the גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a slave sold on condition he serves the seller for thirty days. רבי מאיר says the seller counts as master, because owning the use is like owning the thing, and רבי יהודה says the buyer does, because it is not. רבי יוסי's opinion begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבה's list of three fields
steps.stepSummary: The last two items in רבה's list: a field the husband set aside for her כתובה, and a field she brought into the marriage at an appraised value.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and one field that he set aside for her כתובה, and one field that she brought to him from her own property at an agreed value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבה's list of three fields. If a wife agreed to the sale of one of these, she can later say, 'I only agreed to please my husband.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: These fields are tied to what she will collect if she is divorced or widowed. So a sale of them really hurts her. That is why רבה lets her undo her agreement and say she only went along to keep the peace.

keyTerms.meaning: He set aside or designated (a specific field)
The marriage contract that promises the wife money if she is divorced or widowed
An appraisal: property brought in at a fixed, recorded value
From her own property

phrases.english: and one that he designated for her in her marriage contract,
and one where she brought in to him an appraised field from her own property.
phrases.notes: שׁוּם means the field came into the marriage with a value written down, which the husband is responsible to pay back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement of רבה begun before this point in the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For these fields, a wife's agreement to their sale can be withdrawn by claiming she only agreed to please her husband.

steps.title: What does the list leave out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of property רבה's specific list is meant to exclude.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this list meant to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה named only these three fields. This question sets up the next moves, where answers will be suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A specific list implies that other property follows a different rule. The גמרא wants to know which property that is, so that the list makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
What?

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבה's list is meant to exclude
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which category of property is excluded by רבה's three-field list

steps.title: Not the husband's other property
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: the list excludes the husband's other property. This is rejected, because there she would face even more pressure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes to exclude the rest of his property, that cannot be right. There it is even more true that refusing would cause bad feelings, since he would tell her: 'You are counting on divorce or my death!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer: maybe the list leaves out the husband's other property. It knocks this answer down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she refuses to let him sell his own property, he will accuse her of planning for divorce or his death. So the pressure on her to agree is even stronger there. That means she should certainly be allowed to say 'I only agreed to please him,' and the list cannot be leaving that property out.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
The rest of the property
All the more so
Bad feelings, hostility

phrases.english: If you say: to exclude the rest of the property,
phrases.notes: He means the husband's own property that is held as security for her כתובה.

phrases.english: all the more so there would be hostility for him,
since he would say to her: You have set your eyes
on divorce and on death!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a first answer to the question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבה's list excludes the husband's other property
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pressure on her is even greater with his other property, so her claim should work there too

steps.title: The list leaves out נכסי מלוג
steps.stepSummary: New answer: the list excludes נכסי מלוג, so if she agrees to sell those, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to exclude נכסי מלוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבה's list leaves out נכסי מלוג, the wife's own property that the husband only gets the profits of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So with נכסי מלוג, if she agreed to the sale, she cannot later back out by saying she only wanted to please her husband. This answer is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new answer)
Property that stays the wife's, while the husband eats the profits

phrases.english: Rather, to exclude usufruct property.
phrases.notes: Usufruct property stays hers, but he gets to use it and keep what it produces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The list excludes נכסי מלוג, where her agreement to the sale is binding

steps.title: Challenge from אמימר
steps.stepSummary: אמימר said a sale of נכסי מלוג by husband or wife does nothing at all. So how can her agreement make that sale valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: But אמימר said: a man and woman who sold נכסי מלוג have done nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer using a statement of אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer assumed a sale of נכסי מלוג works when she agrees. אמימר says such a sale accomplishes nothing. So there seems to be nothing for רבה to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)
An אמורא
They did nothing at all; the act has no effect

steps.confusionAlert: Read simply, 'איש ואשה' sounds like both of them sold together. The next step explains that אמימר meant either one selling alone.

phrases.english: But didn't Ameimar say:
a man and a woman who sold usufruct property,
they did not do anything at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a sale of נכסי מלוג with her agreement is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר rules that any sale of נכסי מלוג is void, so there is no valid sale for רבה to exclude

steps.title: אמימר meant one spouse selling alone
steps.stepSummary: אמימר was speaking about a sale by only one spouse. If the husband sold and died, she takes it back. If she sold and died, he takes it back because of a rabbinic enactment.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אמימר's statement was said, it meant this: where he sold and then died, she comes and takes it back. Or where she sold and then died, he comes and takes it back, because of an enactment of the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that אמימר was talking about a case where only one of them sold the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband sells alone, the wife can take the property back after he dies. If the wife sells alone, the husband can take it back after she dies. אמימר's 'nothing at all' is about these one-sided sales. When both agree, the sale can stand, so the answer about נכסי מלוג works again.

keyTerms.meaning: When it was said (it was said about this case)
Takes it out (takes the property back from the buyer)
Or also, alternatively
An enactment made by the Rabbis

phrases.english: When Ameimar's statement was said, it was this:
where he sold and died,
she comes and takes it back;
or also, she sold and died,
he comes and takes it back
by a rabbinic enactment,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing אמימר's case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case (אוקימתא): one spouse selling alone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אמימר meant any sale of נכסי מלוג, even with both agreeing, is void
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר meant only a sale made by one spouse alone

steps.title: The source: the enactment of אושא
steps.stepSummary: The rabbinic enactment is the one רבי יוסי בר חנינא reported. In אושא they ruled that if a wife sold נכסי מלוג and died, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי יוסי בר חנינא, who said: In אושא they made an enactment that if a woman sold נכסי מלוג and then died, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the source of the rabbinic enactment it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's right to take back what his wife sold comes from the enactment made in אושא. This explains the second half of אמימר's case.

keyTerms.meaning: אושא, the town where this enactment was made
They made an enactment
Buyers
Takes back from the hands of

steps.whatToRemember: With נכסי מלוג, a sale by one spouse alone can be undone (אמימר, and the enactment of אושא). But according to this answer, if the wife agreed, she cannot claim 'I only did it to please my husband.' That claim works only for רבה's three fields.

phrases.english: and in line with Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina,
as Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
In Usha they enacted:
a woman who sold usufruct property
and died, the husband takes it back from the buyers;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the source of the rabbinic enactment mentioned in the answer
steps.raayaObject: The husband's right to take back נכסי מלוג his wife sold, once she dies
steps.raayaSupportSource: The enactment of אושא as reported by רבי יוסי בר חנינא

steps.title: When both spouses sell, the sale is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: אמימר's rule only covers a sale by one spouse. If both sell together, or the wife sells to her husband, the sale is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where both of them sold it to someone else, or where she sold it to him, her husband, the sale is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer it began in step 6. It spells out the cases where a sale of נכסי מלוג does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר said a sale by one spouse alone does nothing. When both spouses sell together, every right in the field is being sold, so the sale stands. The same is true when the wife sells to her husband. This explains the earlier reading that her agreement can make a sale valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them, both
To someone else, to an outside buyer
A sale. 'זבינה זביני' means her sale is a real sale

steps.whatToRemember: First answer: אמימר's rule covers a sale by only one spouse. A sale by both spouses, or by the wife to her husband, is valid.

phrases.english: But where the two of them sold to someone else,
or also if she sold it to him,
her sale is a sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the תירוץ from step 6 by naming the cases where the sale is valid.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of אמימר's ruling to a sale by one spouse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אמימר meant that any sale of נכסי מלוג, even by both spouses, is void.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a sale by one spouse alone is void. A sale by both, or by the wife to the husband, is valid.

steps.title: Second answer: אמימר follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A different answer to the question from step 5: אמימר's ruling follows the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: אמימר, who said this, holds like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to answer the question on אמימר. It says his ruling matches the view of רבי אלעזר, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer narrowed אמימר's ruling to a sale by one spouse. This answer goes another way and ties אמימר to a specific opinion. According to this answer, our case follows a different view from his. The ברייתא coming next will show what רבי אלעזר holds about selling something when one person has the item and another has its use.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this opens a second, alternative answer
The אמורא whose ruling on נכסי מלוג is being discussed
A תנא whose view appears in the ברייתא that follows

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second answer to the same question from step 5, offered alongside the first one.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Ameimar, who said this, holds like Rabbi Elazar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 5, in place of the answer given in steps 6 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the ruling to a specific opinion among the תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אמימר's ruling is accepted by everyone, so it contradicts our case.
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר follows רבי אלעזר, so his ruling does not have to fit every view.

steps.title: The ברייתא: selling a slave but keeping his service for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא as a source for רבי אלעזר's view. The case: a man sells his slave on condition that the slave keeps serving him for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: One who sells his slave and agrees with the buyer that the slave will keep serving the seller for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where רבי אלעזר's view comes from. This step sets up the case, and the opinions about it follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case one person owns the slave himself (the buyer) and another person has the slave's work for thirty days (the seller). That is a lot like נכסי מלוג, where the wife owns the field and the husband gets its produce. The ברייתא will ask which master counts as the owner during those thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
His slave (an עבד כנעני)
Made a deal with him, set a condition

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One who sells his slave,
and agreed with him that the slave will serve him for thirty days –
phrases.notes: The slave keeps serving the seller for thirty days before he goes to the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבי אלעזר's view that was mentioned in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That אמימר's ruling fits רבי אלעזר's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a slave sold with thirty days of service kept by the seller

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the first master counts for 'a day or two'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that during the thirty days only the seller falls under the rule of 'a day or two days', because the slave is under his authority. The buyer does not, because the slave is not under his authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The first master falls under the law of 'a day or two days', because the slave is under him. The second master does not fall under the law of 'a day or two days', because the slave is not under him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first opinion in the ברייתא. רבי מאיר says the seller, who is using the slave, is the one treated as his master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says that if a master strikes his slave and the slave lives a day or two before dying, the master is not put to death. רבי מאיר gives this exemption only to the seller, because the slave serves him right now. For רבי מאיר, having the slave's use is what makes someone count as the master.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A day or two days': the rule that a master is exempt if his struck slave lives a day or two
Under him, under his authority
The first master (the seller) / the second master (the buyer)

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא goes on to give other opinions, including רבי אלעזר's. רבי מאיר's view here is the first position the others are measured against.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: הָרִאשׁוֹן יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: The first master is included in the law of 'a day or two days',
phrases.notes: שמות 21:21. A master is exempt if the slave he struck lives a day or two before dying.

phrases.english: because the slave is under him;

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשֵּׁנִי אֵינוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: and the second master is not included in the law of 'a day or two days',
because the slave is not under him –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the case set up in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the thirty days only the seller, who has the slave's service, counts as master for 'a day or two days'. The buyer does not.

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר makes the seller the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's reasoning: he holds that קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that owning the use of something is like owning the thing itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain why רבי מאיר said the seller, and not the buyer, falls under the rule of 'a day or two days'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the thirty days the seller only has the right to the slave's work, which is קנין פירות. רבי מאיר holds that this right counts like full ownership, so the seller is treated as the owner. The buyer, who owns the body of the slave, does not get that status yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (introduces the reasoning behind a view)
Owning the use or profits of something
Owning the thing itself (the body)
Is like, is considered the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the principle that connects the ברייתא back to אמימר's ruling. The question of whether owning the use equals owning the thing is what the sugya is really about.

phrases.english: He holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר from the last step, and now the גמרא is explaining his reasoning.

phrases.english: Ownership of the use is like ownership of the item itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's ruling from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, קנין פירות counts like קנין הגוף.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says the buyer is the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules the opposite way: the buyer falls under 'a day or two days' because the slave is his money, and the seller does not. The גמרא explains that he holds קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the second master (the buyer) falls under the rule of 'a day or two days', because the slave is his money. The first master (the seller) does not, because the slave is not his money. He holds that owning the use of something is not like owning the thing itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second opinion, רבי יהודה, who flips רבי מאיר's ruling. Then the גמרא explains his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה looks at who owns the body of the slave. That is the buyer, so the buyer counts as the owner. The seller only has the right to the slave's work for thirty days, and for רבי יהודה that right is not real ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: The second master, the buyer
The first master, the seller
'A day or two days', the rule about a master who strikes his slave
His money, meaning his property

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: owning the use counts as owning the thing, so the seller is the owner. רבי יהודה: owning the use does not count as owning the thing, so the buyer is the owner.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two masters straight. The 'first' (ראשון) is the seller, who still gets the slave's work for thirty days. The 'second' (שני) is the buyer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: הַשֵּׁנִי יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: The second master is included in the law of 'a day or two days',
because the slave is his money;
phrases.notes: This is the wording of the פסוק itself, שמות 21:21.

phrases.aramaic: הָרִאשׁוֹן אֵינוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: the first master is not included in the law of 'a day or two days',
because the slave is not his money –
He holds:
phrases.notes: Here "he" is רבי יהודה, and the גמרא is explaining his reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: ownership of the use is not like ownership of the item itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא, along with the reasoning behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the buyer is treated as the owner and the seller is not, because קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins quoting רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא introduces a third opinion, רבי יוסי. His actual words come on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. The ברייתא is about to give רבי יוסי's opinion on the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have two opposite views: רבי מאיר says only the seller is the owner, and רבי יהודה says only the buyer is. רבי יוסי's view will add a third approach, but his ruling is not given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the third opinion in this ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third opinion in the same ברייתא, after רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבי יוסי's view. The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
